newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Macraes expects to delay mine expansion.
newsitem.headline: Macraes expects to delay mine expansion.

text.p: Macraes Mining Company said on Thursday it was reviewing its planned gold mining expansion, at its mine at Macraes Flat near Dunedin, after experiencing delays in the local government approvals process and because of the recent fall in the gold price.
The company said the review was expected to defer expansion.
"While Macraes believes the expansion is in the best interests of the project, we believe it is prudent to assess the effects of changed circumstances on it," Macraes said.

The consent hearings for the expansion, which aims to lift gold production to more than 300,000 ounces per year, finished on June 6. Under the Resource Management Act a decision was to have been issued within 15 working days, but the company has been advised it is unlikely a decision will be issued before July 29.

Macraes said that in view of the delay in the approvals process and the overall adverse conditions being experienced in the gold market, it would also undertake a full review of its discretionary expenditures and overheads. The objective was to improve company cashflow and operating cash costs per ounce at Macraes Gold Project.
Macraes said deferring of the expansion would leave it in a very conservative financial position with the ability to move quickly if conditions improved.
It expects to release June quarter report and its proposals arising from the expenditure review in the week of July 28.
